sovereign_country.strategic_role: 拉美西语近岸软件研发外包与数字客服中心

business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Principal AML/CFT framework: Law 599 of 2000 (Criminal Code, Title X – Money Laundering and Financing of Terrorism), Law 526 of 1999 (creates the Financial Information and Analysis Unit – UIAF), Law 1121 of 2006 (AML/CFT measures), Law 1474 of 2011 (anti-corruption statute), Decree 1068 of 2015 (compilatory regulatory decree), and UIAF Resolution 164 of 2021 (mandatory reporting of ultimate beneficial owners to the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales – RUB). For S.A.S. incorporation, Law 1258 of 2008 governs corporate form.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Existence and Legal Capacity of the Foreign Corporate Shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent foreign company registry in the country of origin (e.g., Companies House, Secretary of State)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by competent authority in the country of origin; if the origin country is not a Hague Convention party, Colombian Consular Legalization applies

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney for the Incorporation Representative
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the jurisdiction where the representative resides
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent judicial or foreign affairs authority

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified Copy of Passport and Photo Identification of Each Director, Legal Representative, and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority or Notary Public
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille if notarized; otherwise a certifying officer attests the copy in accordance with origin-country rules

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Criminal Record / Police Clearance for Directors and Legal Representatives (if foreign)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National police or judicial authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or Colombian Consular Legalization if the origin country is not a Hague Convention party

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank Reference Letter for Source of Funds of UBOs
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Financial institution where the UBO maintains the primary account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarized signature and, where required, Hague Apostille; accepted as a due diligence document without apostille when supported by the notary seal

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, directors, legal representatives, and UBOs against the OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council consolidated list, Colombian UIAF terrorist list, and domestic PEP database under SARLAFT/LA/FT (Decreto 1068/2015). Enhanced due diligence is required for foreign and domestic prominent public officials under Law 1474 of 2011. Screening results must be documented and retained for at least ten years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Único Empresarial y Social (RUES) via the Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over the registered domicile; the primary operational portal is www.rues.org.co and for Bogotá www.ccb.org.co
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The corporate name must be written in Spanish and end with the suffix 'S.A.S.'. Foreign words are permissible only if transliterated to Spanish phonetics and if the entire name remains legally pronounceable in Spanish. The name must not contain symbols, logos, or terms that are not alphabetically legible in the RUES database. Accents and the letter 'ñ' are recognized; English-language branding may need to be adapted or accompanied by a Spanish phonetic equivalent.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: words implying government affiliation, regulated financial activity, or a corporate type other than S.A.S.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection by the Cámara de Comercio, the applicant may file a reconsideration appeal (recurso de reposición) before the same chamber within ten (10) business days following notification. If the reconsideration is denied, the applicant may file a subsidiary appeal (recurso de apelación) before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) within five (5) business days. The chamber must resolve the reconsideration within fifteen (15) business days. A successful appeal causes the name to be reactivated in RUES for the remainder of the reservation window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are permitted as a registered domicile for S.A.S. companies provided a local agent for service of process is designated and the by-laws include a physical or notifiable address within Colombia that is legally capable of receiving official correspondence. For low-risk e-commerce activities with no physical inventory in Colombia, a virtual office is acceptable for company registration and annual compliance. The tax administration (DIAN) may request a physical operational address for VAT purposes if the company is inspected, issues invoices with a physical establishment, or holds regulated goods.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Approximately 5% to 8% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection for a low-risk internet retail DTC brand operating with a virtual office and no physical inventory. The probability increases to 15% to 20% if the company registers a commercial establishment, maintains local inventory, or applies for municipal operating licenses.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada); Código de Comercio de Colombia, arts. 110-121 and 373-379; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce) through the Registro Único Empresarial (RUES) and the Superintendencia de Sociedades
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución to be filed and registered with the Cámara de Comercio (public deed required only if real property is contributed)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital under Ley 1258/2008; at least one share must be subscribed and issued; contributions may be cash, assets, or industry and may be paid in full or in instalments as provided in the bylaws; no escrow account or prior capital deposit is required for an e-commerce S.A.S.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [CORPORATE NAME] S.A.S. — At a meeting duly convened on [date], the sole shareholder and initial board resolved: (1) to subscribe and accept the share capital allocation detailed in the incorporation document, authorizing the issue and issuance of shares; (2) to adopt the corporate bylaws and fix the registered office at [address], Bogotá D.C., Colombia; (3) to appoint [Name] as Legal Representative and [Name] as alternate officer, with powers set forth in the bylaws; (4) to authorize the Legal Representative to file all necessary documents with the Cámara de Comercio, DIAN, and other authorities. APPROVED unanimously.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Availability and Bylaws Drafting
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá - 'Consulta de Nombres' window / RUES online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit at least three proposed corporate names to the official RUES name availability engine and verify that the desired S.A.S. name is not identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered entity. After approval, draft the private incorporation document and bylaws in Spanish, including share classes, voting rights, capital subscription, payment term, registered address, legal representative powers, and audit provisions.
required_dossiers: Identity document or passport of each founding shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the preferred name is rejected by the Cámara de Comercio, re-file using the next alternate name from the approved availability list; no fees are forfeited upon resubmission within the same application.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarial Authentication and Execution of Private Incorporation Document
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary Public in the jurisdiction of the company's registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the private incorporation document before a notary for authentication of signatures. All shareholders or their legal representatives must appear in person or through power of attorney. The notary will certify the signatures and return the authenticated private document for submission to the Chamber of Commerce.
required_dossiers: Passport or national ID of all signatories
Power of attorney, if signing through a representative
Proof of domicile/address of legal representatives, if requested
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary refuses authentication due to incomplete identification or inconsistent clauses, correct the document and resubmit; the notarial act may be converted into a public deed at the parties' cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Chamber of Commerce and Issuance of Legal Existence Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio - RUES registration desk or online portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the authenticated private incorporation document with the Cámara de Comercio, along with the completed pre-registration form and the preliminary RUT data. Pay the registration fees calculated on the declared capital. Obtain the Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal, which is the official proof of the company's legal existence and the legal representative's powers.
required_dossiers: Preliminary RUT form issued by DIAN
Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal application
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration is queried or rejected for defects, the Cámara de Comercio will notify the applicant; the company may correct the deficiencies and re-present the document within the legal term (usually 30 calendar days) without incurring additional registration rights for the same capital.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax Registration with DIAN and Obtaining NIT
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales, via the online 'Sede Electrónica'
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After obtaining the Chamber registration certificate, register the company with DIAN to obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and complete the RUT (Registro Único Tributario). Select the appropriate economic activities (ISIC 4791) and register as a responsible party for income tax, VAT, and the presumptive industry and commerce tax regime applicable to e-commerce. All company data must match the Chamber Registry.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RUT is rejected or flags inconsistent data, the legal representative must correct the data through the DIAN online portal and re-submit; a new certificate is issued the same day once the inconsistencies are cleared.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Invoicing Activation and Digital Signature Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: DIAN - electronic invoicing system; authorized certification service providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Procure a digital signature certificate from an authorized CA, register the certificate with DIAN, and activate electronic invoicing ('facturación electrónica') by supplying the required technical and system information. Issue a test electronic invoice to validate the process and obtain the final 'Resolución de Habilitación de Facturación Electrónica' if applicable.
required_dossiers: Email and contact details for DIAN notification
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the electronic invoicing resolution is denied, correct the technical specifications or tax classification and re-apply; temporary invoicing may continue on preprinted forms only with DIAN authorization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Commercial Registration and Land Use Compliance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Municipal Treasury (Secretaría de Hacienda) and Urban Planning Office (Curaduría Urbana) at the registered address
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company's economic activity with the municipal treasury for the industry and commerce tax (ICA under the 'actividad de venta por internet'). If any physical office, storage, or warehouse is used, procure the 'certificado de uso del suelo' confirming that the address permits administrative or light logistics use. For a pure online DTC brand without a physical store, no commercial zoning license is required beyond this municipal activity filing.
required_dossiers: Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal
Lease agreement or proof of ownership of registered address
Certificate of land use (if physical premises)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipal land use certificate is not issued because the address is not zoned for commercial use, obtain a new registered office at a permitted location and update the Chamber Registry and RUT before re-submitting the municipal filing.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — the company operates as a retail sale via internet DTC brand (ISIC 4791) without an industrial or manufacturing plant, so no industrial licensing board approval is required.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: None — a Colombian S.A.S. engaged exclusively in e-commerce is not required to obtain a specific operational manufacturing license; standard tax and municipal commercial registrations suffice.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio de Ambiente y Desarrollo Sostenible / Autoridad Nacional de Licencias Ambientales (ANLA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — the activity is not listed under Decree 1076 of 2015 as requiring an environmental impact assessment or an environmental license, as no physical construction, extraction, manufacturing, or polluting installation is carried out.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Not applicable to an online-only operation; any ancillary office or warehouse must comply with municipal solid waste disposal regulations and, if applicable, the packaging waste take-back obligations under Colombian extended producer responsibility rules for packaging placed on the market.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Not required for a purely virtual e-commerce operation with no staff premises or inventory storage. If the company later leases an office or a fulfillment warehouse, the applicable clearance consists of a fire-safety certificate from the local fire department (Cuerpo de Bomberos) and an occupational health and safety permit under Resolution 0312 of 2019, verified by the ARL (Occupational Risk Administrator).

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT / GST / Sales and Use Tax

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República de Colombia (Central Bank of Colombia), acting through its Junta Directiva and Oficina de Cambios; the foreign-exchange control regime is governed by Decreto 1735 de 1993, Resolución 8 de 2000 (as amended), Circular DCIN-83, and related regulations enforced by authorized Intermediarios del Mercado Cambiario (IMCs) and the DIAN for customs/tax validation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia operates a managed floating exchange-rate system. The Colombian peso (COP) is not pegged, and both current-account and capital-account transactions are generally channelable through authorized IMCs; there is no blanket prohibition on non-resident ownership of a Colombian S.A.S., and 100% foreign shareholding is permitted. Profit remittance is legally free but operationally gated: dividends may only be distributed from audited distributable earnings; the statutory 10% legal reserve (until reaching 50% of subscribed capital) must be appropriated; the shareholders' meeting minutes must evidence the dividend declaration; the remittance must be executed through an IMC with a Declaración de Cambio supported by corporate and tax documentation; and dividends paid to non-residents are typically subject to Colombian withholding taxation (generally 5% on dividends paid out of corporate income already taxed at entity level) with the corresponding DIAN reporting. No central-bank prior authorization is required for the capital outflow itself, but the complete document package is a precondition for the IMC to execute the foreign-currency purchase and remittance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exports of goods, including DTC e-commerce sales fulfilled from Colombia, are designated as obligatory-channeling operations. 100% of the export proceeds must be channeled through the Colombian foreign-exchange market via an authorized IMC within six (6) months from the date of the export declaration/shipment recorded in the Colombian customs export document. Channeling is satisfied by selling the foreign currency to the IMC or by depositing/crediting it to a foreign-currency deposit account (Cuenta en Moneda Extranjera, CME) maintained with an IMC. There is no mandatory percentage-based conversion ratio to COP beyond this full channeling obligation; the exporter may retain the funds in USD in the CME or convert to COP as treasury needs dictate. Proceeds collected through foreign payment aggregators (Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe) must be swept into the IMC channel within the same six-month window and supported by export invoices, shipping evidence, and settlement statements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow / Corporate Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente) plus Foreign-Currency Deposit Account (CME)
Capital Escrow / Corporate Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente) plus Foreign-Currency Deposit Account (CME)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility Rating: Low as a final treasury repository; Medium as a temporary liquidity aggregator. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Airwallex, Mercury, Revolut Business) are not licensed Colombian IMCs and cannot replace the mandatory canalización of export proceeds. Funds held in offshore EMIs without being swept to a Colombian IMC within the statutory export channeling window breach Resolución 8 de 2000 and expose the S.A.S. to foreign-exchange sanctions. EMIs may be used as intermediate collection tools for Shopify/PayPal/Stripe settlement proceeds, provided that the balances are repatriated to an IMC account within the six-month window and that the merchant maintains a complete audit trail showing the underlying customer transactions, settlement reports, and the onward wire to the IMC. Use of offshore EMIs for outbound supplier payments without first channeling is also disallowed when those proceeds originate from Colombian export operations.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Colombian tier-1 banks generally require the legal representative to appear physically or through a notarized special power of attorney (poder especial) granted to a local attorney or domiciled officer; powers granted abroad must be apostilled and legally translated. Remote onboarding through video calls and biometric verification is increasingly available at Bancolombia, Banco de Bogotá, and BBVA Colombia for low-risk local S.A.S. entities, but foreign-owned holding structures are routinely routed to an enhanced in-person or notarized KYC interview. Under Law 2069 of 2020, S.A.S. formation documents may be executed through distance/facial-recognition signature mechanisms, but banks retain a stricter internal KYC mandate and often still require a physical appearance by the legal representative or an attorney-in-fact. Practical mandate: arrange for at least one director or a locally domiciled authorized agent to complete a face-to-face or hybrid notarized onboarding ceremony, and prepare the corporate, tax, and UBO documentation in advance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Payment aggregator inflows (Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe) arriving as high-velocity, small-ticket USD settlements without a corresponding Declaración de Cambio, flagged by SARLAFT as unclassified cross-border card-not-present flows.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the bank with monthly settlement statements from each aggregator; the e-commerce platform identification (Shopify store URL and seller credentials); matching commercial invoices and shipping/customs export declarations; proof that net settlements were re-channeled to the IMC account; and the IMC-issued Declaración de Cambio receipts showing the applicable export concept code. A documented reconciliation spreadsheet tracing each settlement batch to the corresponding export invoice is essential.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity: non-resident shareholders controlling the S.A.S. through an offshore holding company, triggering enhanced due diligence and non-resident red flags.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: File and certify the Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales (RUBF) with the DIAN; provide apostilled corporate registry certificates and constitutional documents of the entire ownership chain; deliver a UBO attestation signed by the local legal representative; include source-of-funds and source-of-wealth statements for the non-resident shareholders; and present the notarized capital contribution minutes evidencing the true beneficial owners.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High volume of small-ticket card-not-present transactions and chargeback activity creating a pattern consistent with carding, account-takeover, or money-moulding typologies.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver a fraud and chargeback management report (Shopify Fraud Control, Signifyd or equivalent); a refund/chargeback ledger; customer acquisition and advertising funnel evidence (Google/Meta ads); order metadata demonstrating ordinary retail purchasing behavior; and a geographic customer profile consistent with truthfully marketed DTC operations. If high-risk jurisdictions appear, show geo-blocking safeguards and a sanctions-screening process.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Mismatch between the RUT (tax registration) principal activity code and the actual foreign-exchange flows, causing the bank's transaction-monitoring system to flag inconsistent trade narratives.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Update the RUT with ISIC 4791 (retail sale via Internet) as the principal activity and add complementary codes for digital trade support and logistics; maintain consistent filing of DIAN export information and VAT returns; align the purpose descriptions on all incoming wires with the underlying export contracts; and keep a standing treasury file mapping each FX operation to the relevant Declaración de Cambio concept code and supporting export/import documents.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Equity capital and shareholder loans from non-residents must enter Colombia exclusively through an authorized IMC. Recommended protocol: route a SWIFT MT103 from the shareholder's bank to the S.A.S.'s operational account at a tier-1 Colombian bank, using the beneficiary company's NIT as the beneficiary identifier and including an unambiguous originator-to-beneficiary information (OBI) field describing 'Aporte de capital - Inversión directa de capital' or 'Préstamo entre compañías', matched to the notarized share subscription minutes or loan agreement. The receiving IMC must file the Declaración de Cambio (Formulario No. 1) using the appropriate foreign investment or external debt concept code. Within the statutory registration window (in current Banco de la República practice, generally up to twelve months from the investment date), the S.A.S. must register the investment in the Registro de Inversiones Internacionales; for shareholder loans, the external debt registration requirements must also be met. Documentation required: corporate existence certificate, RUT, apostilled share subscription minutes, source-of-funds certification from the non-resident shareholder, and the bank's SWIFT credit advice.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For an e-commerce DTC brand, outbound disbursements comprise supplier invoices, logistics fees, advertising costs (Google/Meta), software subscriptions, and payment-processor fees. The preferred clearing rail is SWIFT MT103 executed through an authorized IMC, with each transaction supported by the underlying contract/invoice and a Declaración de Cambio where channeling obligations apply. For high-value inventory purchases, a commercial letter of credit governed by UCP 600 issued by a tier-1 local bank is appropriate, with required documents being proforma invoice, transport document, insurance certificate, and inspection certificate where applicable. For recurring low-value programmatic payments (SaaS, advertising, logistics), aggregate settlement through the IMC with a monthly reconciliation file is acceptable; corporate virtual cards may be used only where the issuing bank records the transaction as a foreign-exchange operation and provides a statement that supports the Declaración de Cambio. Do not use informal aggregators, personal cards, or direct transfers from offshore EMIs as substitutes for the IMC rail when the underlying funds are Colombian export proceeds subject to canalización.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore deliverable COP/USD forex forward contracts with authorized Colombian IMCs, used to hedge receivables and payables denominated in foreign currency; requires documented underlying trade exposure.

Offshore COP/USD non-deliverable forwards (NDFs), permissible for hedging where onshore market depth is insufficient; settled in USD without physical delivery of COP and must be documented as hedge transactions to avoid speculative classification.
Cross-currency swaps (COP/USD) with local or international bank counterparties, permissible for hedging long-term foreign-currency debt or capital-injection exposures.

Vanilla foreign-exchange options purchased from authorized IMCs, permissible as hedging instruments for contingent pricing or procurement exposure; writing/selling options by non-financial corporate entities is generally not recommended and may be treated as speculative under Colombian FX regulations.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Commercial Registry Renewal (Renovación de la Matrícula Mercantil)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (local Chamber of Commerce with jurisdiction over registered office, e.g., Bogotá)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by March 31 for companies with a December 31 fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers COP surcharges (approx. USD 15-150) and access restrictions on company records; three consecutive years of non-renewal exposes the entity to administrative cancellation/strike-off from the Commercial Registry under Co. Commercial Code Art. 238.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Shareholders' Meeting and Filing of Meeting Minutes (Asamblea Ordinaria de Accionistas)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio (minutes of the assembly must be filed with the Commercial Registry)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Meeting must be held and minutes filed by March 31 following the preceding December 31 fiscal year end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to convene and file minutes may void corporate resolutions, delay registration of subsequent acts, and expose officers to fines; chronic non-compliance may trigger intervention by the Superintendencia de Sociedades.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Owner Confirmation (Registro Único de Beneficiarios Finales - R-UBO)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually within three months of fiscal year end (by March 31); any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial title must be updated within 30 calendar days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing, incorrect data, or omitted beneficial owners attract DIAN penalties of up to COP 50,000,000 or 5% of equity, per Colombian Tax Code Art. 651; repeated non-filing may also trigger the freezing of extraordinary transactions with the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Tax Third-Party Information Return (Información Exógena)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually by June 30 of the following fiscal year; only applicable when the e-commerce S.A.S. exceeds DIAN size/turnover thresholds for reporting payment and sales data
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing or incomplete filing exposes the company to fines of up to 5% of the reported value or 20% of the omitted value, plus extraterritorial surcharges under Colombian Tax Code Art. 651.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory under Colombian Commercial Code Art. 28 when total gross assets or gross revenues exceed 5,000 SMLMV (approx. COP 7,117,500,000 / USD 1.65 million for 2025); S.A.S. entities below these thresholds are exempt unless required by by-laws, a qualified equity interest, or the Superintendencia de Sociedades order.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Decreto 2420 de 2015 (Marco Técnico Normativo): full IFRS for Grupo 1 entities, IFRS for SMEs for Grupo 2 entities, or the simplified micro-entity framework for Grupo 3; the typical digital retail S.A.S. with no significant public-interest status applies the Grupo 2 IFRS for SMEs framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The S.A.S. must file its annual R-UBO confirmation with DIAN before March 31 of each year; every shareholding transfer, pledge, or repurchase is reportable within 30 days and must identify any individual ultimately owning or controlling 10% or more of the share capital or exercising a management or control interest; dormant entities with no reportable shareholders are still required to submit a nil confirmation.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Accionistas / Registro de Acciones)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Junta Directiva)
Minute Book for Shareholders' Meetings (Libro de Actas de Asamblea)
Register of Contributions and Capital (Registro de Aportes y Capital Suscrito)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 - 800 per year for registered office, virtual office and company agent services in Bogotá, Medellín or other commercial hubs
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 - 6,000 per year where a Revisor Fiscal is mandatory; no external audit fee required for small S.A.S. below the 5,000 SMLMV threshold

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general tax holiday. Available incentives include (i) deduction of 50% of fees paid to qualifying creative/software service providers under the Orange Economy Law (Law 1955/2019) subject to certification; (ii) tax-loss carryforward offsetting future taxable income; (iii) VAT neutrality for exported digital services. Standard DTC domestic sales activity remains fully taxable at 35%.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 — Official corporate income tax return 'Declaración de Renta y Complementarios' filed electronically via the DIAN 'Muisca' portal; authentication via digital certificate or key.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual. The fiscal year is the calendar year, with a single yearly return; no quarterly income tax declarations for standard S.A.S. entities.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The return is due within 180 calendar days after year-end; DIAN fixes specific deadlines by the last two digits of the NIT between early March and late April of the following year. No extension is available for foreign-owned S.A.S. entities.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter the S.A.S.'s 9-digit NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria), legal name, and corporate email.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The non-resident shareholders must be identified through the tax agent or legal representative; provide their foreign tax ID and country of residence in the appendix schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Report all gross income derived from the DTC webstore, including Shopify, PayPal and Stripe transaction settlements before platform fees and sales returns.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Amounts received from Colombian and foreign customers via e-commerce are taxable as Colombian-source income; exchange rate conversion is based on the DIAN periodic exchange rate (TRM).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 47 — Costs and Deductions (Costos y Deducciones)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Record cost of goods sold (or cost of digital product licences), merchant fees, logistics, marketing, hosting, payroll and applicable depreciation/amortization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign payments for services or royalties must be supported by documented withholding tax (WHT) certificates and must comply with transfer-pricing documentation if above the threshold.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 55 — Taxable Income before Net Losses (Renta Líquida)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Derive net taxable income after subtracting deductions and exempt revenues from gross income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident-owned S.A.S. entities may not deduct deemed equity interest cancelation expenses unless the profit-sharing is economically substantiated.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 60 — Corporate Income Tax Rate (Tarifa de Renta)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Apply the 35% statutory rate to the taxable income in Box 55.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: No reduced general rate applies for non-residents; treaty relief under a DTA, if any, is recognized through Box 70/79 foreign tax credits or remittance WHT schedules.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 63 — Income Tax Payable (Impuesto de Renta a Cargo)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Calculate Renta Líquida × 35%; then subtract prepayments, withholdings and credits to obtain net tax payable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Tax prepayments made during the year must be reconciled; non-resident shareholders cannot claim Colombian personal expenses as credits.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 72 — Foreign Tax Credit (Descuento Tributario por Impuestos Pagados en el Exterior)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Enter income taxes paid abroad that are creditable under Article 254/255 of the Tax Code, supported by TRC; credit cannot exceed the Colombian income tax attributable to that foreign-source income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For foreign-owned entities, any DTA-reduced WHT on outbound royalty/interest is administered as a withholding declaration, not as a foreign tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 90 — Total Liability or Balance in Favor
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final position: if taxes withheld by third parties exceed tax due, the difference is a 'saldo a favor' available for compensation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: S.A.S. with only expenses and no Colombian source income should still file a zero-liability return; failure to file is penalized.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing: penalty of 5% for each month of delay on the tax discharged up to 100%; failure to file when no tax is payable incurs an ART penalty of up to 200 UVT (approx COP 9,413,000 in 2024); default interest of ~2.4% per month accrues from the original due date; erroneous or false returns trigger penalties of 20% of the understated amount.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% final withholding tax on dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders, withheld and remitted by the Colombian S.A.S.; no further Colombian income tax if the dividends were paid out of already-taxed corporate profits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a DTA reduction, the non-resident shareholder must supply a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) issued by the beneficial owner's residence tax authority for the calendar year, accompany the dividend remittance with a beneficial ownership declaration and the underlying DTA schedule, and have the Colombian S.A.S. file the withholding declaration with DIAN before payment. Treaty rates are not automatic; formal approval is processed through the withholding mechanism and can be audited.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory: royalties for patented/coded IP 15%; interest paid to banks/foreign lenders 15%; general non-domiciled services 15%. Treaty rates typically 10% or 5% for interest/royalties under Colombia's comprehensive DTAs (e.g. Chile, Spain, Mexico, Canada, South Korea). Royalties paid to related parties are additionally subject to transfer-pricing analysis; excess interest may be recharacterized as dividend (10% WHT) under thin capitalization rules.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File: mandatory for the S.A.S. if (i) gross income in the fiscal year exceeds 150,000 UVT (approx COP 7,060 million for 2024) or (ii) total assets exceed 150,000 UVT, or (iii) related-party transactions exceed 100,000 UVT (approx COP 4,706 million). Master File: mandatory if the foreign group consolidated annual gross income exceeds 200,000 UVT (approx COP 9,410 million) and the local entity carries out related-party transactions. A CbC Report is required for groups with consolidated income ≥ 2,000,000 UVT.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia has no separate Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) analogous to the UAE/CRS regimes, but the Tax Code (Articles 894 and 899) and jurisprudence empower DIAN to disregard form over substance, recharacterize loans, and deny deductions where the S.A.S. lacks real activity, personnel and risk control. A passive invoice-hosting shell with no human/economic footprint cannot rely on formal incorporation to protect its tax benefits.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion / Omission of Global E-commerce Revenues
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Underdeclaring or failing to report Shopify, PayPal or Stripe sales settlements; maintaining separate undisclosed bank accounts; manipulating TRM conversion or using non-audited bookkeeping to reduce Renta Líquida.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Income tax deficiency of 35% plus monthly default interest; inaccuracy penalty of 20% of the understated gross amount; criminal tax evasion sanctions under Article 435 of the Colombian Penal Code: imprisonment between 48 and 108 months and a fine equal to 50%-200% of the evaded tax. The S.A.S. may lose its NIT and be removed from the DIAN registry.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Veil-piercing applies to legal representatives who intentionally sign false returns; they are jointly and severally liable with the S.A.S. for the evaded tax, interest, and penalties; travel bans, preventive embargoes on personal assets, and passport revocation are available. Imprisonment terms attach to the natural person, not the legal entity.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Sham / Shell Arrangement without Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the S.A.S. purely as a nominal 'letterbox' for foreign DTC commerce — no employees, no physical office, no board decisions in Colombia, no commercial risk; artificially interposing the S.A.S. between foreign shareholders and Colombian customers to gain tax benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN may disregard the entity's separate legal personality under Article 894 via an administrative audit, reassess taxes to the actual beneficial owner, impose penalties equal to 200% of the omitted tax plus advance payments, and cancel the S.A.S.'s NIT for prolonged non-compliance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who act without corporate purpose or knowingly permit sham transactions are jointly liable without limitation; personal bank accounts may be attached; a director may face a migration ban while the administrative investigation is pending and criminal charges for ideological false statement to the registry.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving settlement funds through anonymous payment channels, using third-party mystery customer payment structures, layering funds across crypto wallets or shell accounts to conceal the e-commerce proceeds; failing to implement basic KYC/CDD as required by UIAF for payment aggregators.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering (Arts. 323-324 Penal Code) sanctions: imprisonment of 8 to 18 years and fines equivalent to 1 to 50% of the assets laundered; UIAF fine up to COP 200 million for failure to report unusual transactions; criminal confiscation of the DTC brand proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers are criminal co-principals if they knowingly omit reports or tolerate layering; travel bans, extradition risk, and freeze of personal estates in Colombia. The company’s registration with the UIAF is suspended, effectively blocking all payment rails.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Paying excessive management, IP licensing, marketing or logistics fees to a foreign related party; charging no or low arm's-length margins for functions actually performed in Colombia; using thin capitalization (debt-to-equity beyond the 3:1 safe harbour) to erode the Colombian tax base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN TP adjustment increases taxable income to arm's length level; a 15% withholding is re-applied on deemed remittances; accuracy penalty of 20% of the TP adjustment; denial of deductions and tariff surcharge on hidden dividends. Criminal liability if TP documentation is intentionally falsified.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative is jointly liable for TP adjustments arising from transactions he/she approved with a related party; liability extends to directors’ personal estates if the S.A.S. is insolvent; criminal imprisonment up to 96 months for falsifying Local File documentation or destroying underlying transaction records.
